Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. We will pause for a moment to give everyone an opportunity to signal for questions. Thank you. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings' results for the third quarter. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. Overall, the company posted record revenue growth and strong profitability amid a challenging environment. We made significant progress on our efficiency ratio, capital ratios, and risk-weighted assets management. Deposit growth remained robust across transactional, savings, and time deposits, while our macroeconomic outlook supports continued momentum. Finally, we're optimistic about loan growth and credit quality going forward.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $1.4 billion for the third quarter, or $0.98 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 10% year-over-year driven by higher loan balances and net interest margin expansion to 3.45%. Non-interest income was up 7%, reflecting strong performance in investment banking fees and wealth management. Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Let me expand on our overall company performance highlights first. This quarter capped a banner year so far for GlobalBank Holdings, underscoring our resilience amid the Federal Reserve's higher-for-longer rate stance at 5.25-5.50%, inflation around 3%, and geopolitical tensions. We delivered total revenue of $4.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 8% excluding market gains—our strongest growth since 2019. Net interest income surged 18% to $3.1 billion, with NIM expanding 25 basis points to 3.45%, thanks to our asset-sensitive structure and deposit betas at 65%. Non-interest revenue rose 4% to $1.0 billion, driven by 15% growth in investment banking fees where we ranked high in U.S. league tables, and record wealth management AUM of $1.2 trillion, up 22% with $18 billion in net inflows.

Adjusted net income hit $1.4 billion, up 15%, with diluted EPS of $0.98 beating estimates. ROTCE reached 14.5%, matching top peers, and ROA improved to 1.25%. Credit quality was pristine: net charge-offs at 28 basis points, delinquencies at 0.95%, and provision expense low at $250 million after reserve releases. Loans grew 8% to $285 billion, led by 12% in C&I and 10% in residential mortgages. Deposits rose 6% to $420 billion, with core at 48%. LCR at 125%, CET1 at 13.2%.

By segment, Consumer & Business Banking revenue up 10% to $1.8 billion on 15% digital deposit growth; Commercial Banking up 14% to $1.3 billion; Wealth & Investment up 16% to $0.7 billion; Markets steady. U.S. grew 13%, Asia-Pacific 20%. Tech investments like AI fraud detection saved $150 million, cloud migration cut IT costs 15%, and UniPay wallet added 5 million users.

For 2024, we guide mid-single-digit revenue growth, stable NIM, ROTCE 14-15%, $1.5 billion buybacks, and 10% dividend hike.

Turning to our efficiency ratio, a key metric of operational discipline. It's non-interest expenses over total revenue, lower better. We hit 58.2% in Q3, 370 basis points better year-over-year from 61.9%, and 110 basis points sequential improvement—our best since post-pandemic. Full-year so far beats sub-60% target. Expenses grew 2.1% to $4.2 billion vs. 8.4% revenue to $7.2 billion. Savings from 15% vendor cuts with FIS/Temenos, $150 million procurement. Tech: AWS core platform automated 40% back-office via RPA; GlobalBank AI Advisor handles 25% inquiries, saving $80 million; ML fraud cut false positives 30%, $120 million preserved. Headcount down 7% to 45,000, redeployed to wealth/ESG.

Regionally: North America 56.8% on 5.2% deposit growth; Europe 61.5% but improved 250 bps via 120 branch closures; Asia-Pacific 54.2% on trading and fintech like Grab, 28% digital lending. 2024 target 57% or better, H2 sub-57%, mid-50s by 2026 with NIM at 3.45% up 25 bps, fees to 35%. Investments in GenAI for 20% cross-sell, BaaS like Goldman Marcus. CET1 12.8% buffers risks.

Next, capital ratios. CET1 at 13.2% fully loaded Basel III, up 40 bps QoQ and 110 bps YoY—strongest improvement lately. Tier 1 15.1%. Exceeds U.S. 10.5% req (4.5% Pillar 1, 2.5% buffer, 3.5% G-SIB), plus buffers for 250 bps headroom. Europe 11.2% req, we're 13.2%; Asia 14.1%. YTD +110 bps from $4.2 billion retained earnings, net of dividends/repurchases. RWA up 1.2% to $1.05 trillion, offset by de-risking: credit +2%, market -5%.

Optimized via IFRS 9 ECL 10 bps dilution; Basel IV models shaved 15 bps on CRE; securitized $15 billion autos; SRT on $10 billion. North America 13.5% post-CCAR; Europe 13.0%; Asia 14.1%. Positions for $3-5 billion M&A, $5 billion buyback, 10% dividend to $1.20, 40-50% payout.

On risk-weighted assets management, total RWA $785 billion, down 2.1% QoQ, 0.8% YoY—sixth straight quarter. Intensity 42.5% vs. peers 45-48%. Credit RWA 82% at $644 billion, -2.4%; market -1.8% to $59 billion; op +0.5% to $82 billion. North America -3.2% via $12 billion maturities, $4.5 billion CRE sale. Europe flat, IRB relief 15% on mortgages. Asia +1.5% low-RWA trade finance.

Capital Velocity Framework: AI scenarios target 5-7% annual reduction. Divested $22 billion high-RWA; ML IRB 6% shave on corporates; FRTB models 12% cut; $8 billion synth sec; CDS hedging. Op risk via AI monitoring. 2025 guide $770-790 billion, CET1 to 13.5%.

Deposit growth and mix: Up 8.2% YoY to $285 billion, beating industry 4-5%. Core 78%. Transactional $112 billion, 39%, +3.1% QoQ on C&I/SMB treasury, app 4.2 million users. Savings $102 billion, 36%, +11.5% on 4.75% HYSA, $4.8 billion inflows. Time $71 billion, 25%, +22% at 4.60%, brokered 18%. Cost 2.85%, LCR 145%. Trends: 4% shift to interest-bearing, D/L 92%. Strategies: AI optimizers +28% conversion; cross-sell 65%; regional digital/hedging. Guide 6-8% FY growth.

Macro outlook: Global GDP 3.1%, advanced 1.7%, U.S. CPI 2.9%. Fed two cuts '24, 75 bps '25 to 3.75-4%. U.S. consumer strong, unemployment 4.1%, mortgages $15.2 billion. CRE watch: 1.2% delinquency, de-risked urban. Europe ECB cuts boost SME; Asia India 22% digital, China ringfenced. NII $2.1 billion +9%, fees +6%, NPLs 0.95%. GenAI cross-sell +15%. Guide 4-6% loans, NIM 3.45-3.55%, ROE 13-14%.

Finally, outlook for loan growth and credit quality. Loans +5-6% FY24 from Q3 $285 billion. C&I 6-8% on manufacturing/tech; CRE 2-4% multifamily/industrial, office contained; Consumer 7% mortgages/autos. AI platform -30% cycle times. Credit: past-due 0.85%, NCO 22 bps, Q4 25-30 bps. Provisions $250-300 million, coverage 1.45%. Base soft landing, risks buffered by CECL models.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, cybersecurity threats, and geopolitical risks. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including enhanced stress testing and hedging strategies.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.95% and net charge-offs at 28 basis points. We are actively managing our loan portfolio, particularly the commercial real estate segment, which has performed resiliently with low delinquencies. We remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of our GlobalBank AI Advisor, which has seen rapid customer adoption with 25% of inquiries handled autonomously and substantial efficiency gains in operations and fraud prevention.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include our procurement optimization program delivering $150 million in run-rate savings and branch rationalization with 120 closures, which are contributing to improved productivity and cost savings.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into the progress on your efficiency ratio and targets?

John Reynolds:
Thanks, Mike. As Michael detailed, we're thrilled with the 58.2% ratio this quarter, a 370 basis point year-over-year improvement driven by expense discipline, tech efficiencies like our AI advisor and RPA, and workforce optimization. Regionally strong, targeting 57% for 2024 and mid-50s by 2026, funding growth investments without cutting corners.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your plans for capital deployment and returns given the strong CET1 levels?

Michael Chen:
Great question, Emily. With CET1 at 13.2% and 250 bps buffer, we're prioritizing shareholder returns with $5 billion incremental buyback targeting 1.5% yield, 10% dividend increase to $1.20, and $3-5 billion M&A for fintech bolt-ons. Organic accretion keeps us at 13.5-14% year-end, resilient in stress tests.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
How are you managing risk-weighted assets amid Basel IV and Endgame rules?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, David. We've reduced RWA 2.1% QoQ to $785 billion via our Capital Velocity Framework—portfolio sales, model enhancements, securitizations. Proactive ahead of output floors and Endgame uplift, maintaining low intensity at 42.5%, supporting growth and returns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Green with Wells Fargo Securities. Please go ahead.

Rachel Green:
Can you discuss the performance of your deposit franchise and loan growth outlook?

David Kim:
Hi Rachel. Deposits grew 8.2% to $285 billion with stable mix and low betas; strategies like AI optimizers and cross-sell driving inflows. Loans outlook 5-6%, balanced across C&I, CRE, consumer, with pristine quality—NCOs 22 bps, strong coverage—positioned for risk-adjusted expansion.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
